cells.B6: A career-mode companion for EA SPORTS FC 27: the full player database (19,789 players, Launch data, Sept 2026), FC27-style deal structuring, season finances, and an FFP monitor with real rules for every league in the game.
cells.B9: 1.  Set Up - pick your club. League, cups, home nation, registration rules and financial rules fill in automatically (the League Rules sheet explains them for your league), and so do the season-1 transfer and wage budgets, club balance, stadium capacity and facility levels - from FMInside's Football Manager 26 data for your club. Type over any of them. To get an FMInside figure back, clear it (apps) or press FILL FROM FMINSIDE on Set Up (Excel).
cells.B10: 2.  Squad - press IMPORT SQUAD FROM DB. Your club's players appear with ratings, values, wages and contracts; the season-1 wage budget rises to the imported wage bill if it is lower. Then set List A/B, roles and any wages you renegotiate. The registration panel shows only the rules your league actually has, plus the UEFA squad list in seasons you play in Europe.
cells.B11: The workbook starts on Season 0 - pre-season setup. When your club, budgets and squad are in, press START NEW SEASON once: that locks the setup in and starts season 1 (nothing is archived).
cells.B12: 3.  Play. Plan deals on the Deal Structurer and press LOG THIS SIGNING / LOG THIS SALE - cash, installments and amortisation then flow through Finances and the FFP monitor.
cells.B13: 4.  At the end of each season fill the END OF SEASON panel on the Dashboard (league position, league outcome, W-D-L, goals, cup and continental results, other trophies, next season's continental competition) and press START NEW SEASON. It writes the season into Season Stats, switches league after promotion or relegation (FFP and registration rules follow), ages every player a year, moves players who are too old off List B, lists contracts that have ended, moves player stats to Season Stats and recalculates next season's budgets. Optionally fill the light-blue Finances rows from the game's finance screen. In the macro-free .xlsx, fill the Season Stats row and change 'Current season #' by hand instead.
cells.B16: You never type the budgets after season 1. Next season's modifier comes from how the season ended: promoted +30%, won the league +10%, Europe / top quarter +5%, top half 0%, bottom half -5%, relegated -25%. Wage budget = the larger of last season's wage budget and closing wage bill, x the modifier. Transfer budget = whatever you didn't spend last season + new money from the board (the season-1 budget grown by the modifiers, halved while the club is in debt). Both are on Finances > Budgets, with override rows if your game gives a different figure.
cells.B19: Light-blue cells with blue text are yours to edit. Everything else is calculated - sheets are protected with no password (Review > Unprotect Sheet if you really need to). Squad depth: red = nobody, amber = one player, light green = two, green = three or more (the Dashboard chart uses the same colours). Academy depth: grey = empty, green = one or two, red = more than the house-rule maximum of two.
cells.B22: The Squad panel shows only the rules your league actually has, plus the UEFA squad list in seasons you play in Europe. List B is decided by birth year (e.g. Premier League and UEFA 2026/27: born 2005 or later); in LALIGA only academy (B-team) players qualify. Eligibility = Loaned Out / Unregistered removes a player from the counts. Dual Nat. = Y exempts a player from the foreign quota (EU or home passport, MLS green card). Players from Cotonou-agreement countries (most of Africa and the Caribbean) are not non-EU in Spain and France.
cells.B25: Dashboard: START NEW SEASON; UPGRADE buttons next to each facility and the stadium (asks the cost, raises the level, posts the cost to Finances).
cells.B26: Set Up: RESET WORKBOOK (red) - clears every log and roster for a new save; Set Up is kept. Double confirmation, cannot be undone.
cells.B27: Squad: IMPORT SQUAD FROM DB; LOG SALE OF SELECTED (sells the player on the row you have selected).
cells.B28: Deal Structurer: WILL HE SIGN? (ROLL) and LOG THIS SIGNING for a player you are buying; WILL HE STAY? (ROLL) and LOG THIS SALE for one of yours. The selling side's roll asks whether a rival bid unsettles him: a bad roll means he forces a sale or refuses to renew (Refused Deal = Y on the Squad sheet).
cells.B31: Deal Structurer > CONTRACT RENEWAL: pick one of your players to see his contract, the role his rating earns him in your squad, the market wage for his rating in your league (median FC27 wage of players rated within 1 of him) and his demand for the role you offer (the larger of his wage +5% and the market wage, scaled by the role). Set role, wage, years and any signing bonus to see the wage-budget, transfer-budget, salary-cap, pay-limit and FFP effect, and the chance he accepts (house rule: wage vs demand, role vs expected role, his happiness, nationality bonus; 0% once he has refused). WILL HE RENEW? (ROLL) is optional; LOG THIS RENEWAL writes the new wage, contract year and role to the Squad sheet and posts the bonus to the Finances ledger.
cells.B32: Youth Academy: PROMOTE (ROLL), RELEASE, SIGN YOUTH PLAYER (ROLL) and ADD WITHOUT ROLL. Signing takes the name, position, age, nationality and the rating/potential ranges from your scout's report and adds him to the academy list.
cells.B35: Your league's rules in plain words - squad registration and player eligibility, foreign and home-grown quotas, UEFA lists, the financial (FFP) test and the salary cap - each with your squad checked against it. It always shows your current league and follows Set Up's overrides; after promotion or relegation it switches with you.
cells.B38: The Dashboard's FFP & SALARY CAP strip shows your league's test live: the limit, where you are now, the room left a year and a week, and how much of the limit you have used. Salary-cap leagues use your squad's cap figure; squad-cost-ratio and wages-to-turnover leagues use this season's revenue. FC27 doesn't show club revenue, so when the Finances income rows are blank it is estimated from your wage budget and the share of revenue your league's clubs typically spend on wages (shown in italics on FFP & Rules). Type FC27's figures on Finances to replace the estimate.
cells.B41: The Squad panel, Set Up and League Rules follow the competition you play: UEFA (25-man List A, 8 locally trained, unlimited under-21 List B), CONMEBOL Libertadores / Sudamericana (50-player list), AFC Champions League Elite / Two (25 + an under-21 List B of up to 10, 6 home-grown places) and the CONCACAF Champions Cup (35-man roster). In a season without one, your confederation's main competition is shown for reference. UEFA's financial rules apply only in UEFA seasons.
cells.B44: Caps run in FC27 money. FC27 pays each league on its own scale (NWSL squads earn about three times their real salaries, Serie B squads a fraction), so every amount is the real 2026/27 figure x the league's in-game wage scale (Set Up rows 73-74, real figures beside them). Hard caps that every real club must meet (MLS, NWSL, A-League) are scaled so every FC27 club starts within the limit; limits that follow each club's money (LALIGA, Segunda, Turkey, Serie B, China) by FC27's league wage bill / the real one, or by the club's own ratio where its real payroll is known (it follows the club after relegation); per-player pay limits so nobody starts over them. Serie B's ceiling is soft: going over needs a bank guarantee for part of the excess (40% in 2026/27, rising 10 points a season to 70%), shown as GUARANTEE rather than BREACH. Limits update every season: league-wide caps grow on their published schedules (MLS, NWSL); each club's own limit (LALIGA, Segunda, Turkey) moves with your revenue if you type it, otherwise with your results (the same finish modifiers as the budgets); Serie B ceilings follow each club's status (relegated, promoted) season by season. Type your own scale on Set Up (1.00 = real-world money).
cells.B45: Where a league has a salary cap, the Squad sheet shows your cap figure, the limit and the room left, the Deal Structurer shows whether a signing still fits under the cap (and any per-player pay limit), and the Dashboard shows the room. The cap figure follows the league's rules: MLS counts only the 20 highest earners and charges each of its 3 Designated Players a flat charge, with GAM/TAM allocation money as extra room; NWSL adds the High Impact Player room; the A-League has one marquee outside the cap plus designated-player room; CSL also caps each player's pay (home and foreign) and all foreign wages together; Serie B has club-by-club ceilings and a higher one after relegation; LALIGA and Turkish clubs have their own published limits. At each season end the squad's cap figure is saved for the FFP monitor.
cells.B48: The signing chances (Deal Structurer, rival bids, youth signings) include a nationality bonus: a player is keener on a club in his home nation (x1.30) or in a country that speaks one of his languages (x1.15) - Argentines to Spain, Brazilians to Portugal, Senegalese to France, Austrians to Germany, Scandinavians to each other. The same bonus makes him harder to prise away from such a club. Both multipliers are on Set Up (set them to 1.00 to switch it off).
cells.B51: The green ROLL buttons are optional realism dice - FC27 already runs its own negotiations, so only roll if you want extra uncertainty on top. Facility levels and upgrades, squad-role targets and the max youth-scout stars are also community house rules: FC27 has no facility upgrade screen. The signing-chance model is carried over from the FC26 community spreadsheet.
cells.B54: Installments (% deferred over 1-5 years), sign-on and agent fees, contingent add-ons (only count once you log them as paid), player exchanges, sell-on % given or kept (owed sell-ons are deducted automatically when you sell), buy-back and release clauses, loans. Profit on sale uses the player's remaining book value - the way FFP rules measure it.
cells.B57: 70 and 85 are NOT salary caps. They are squad cost ratios: squad cost (wages + amortisation) as a % of revenue + player-sale profit. 85% is the Premier League and Championship rule from 26/27; 70% is UEFA's, which only applies in seasons you play in Europe. Other leagues use their own test: a squad cost ratio (Serie A 70%, Belgium 80%, Saudi Arabia 75%), wages vs turnover (League One 50%, League Two 55%, Ligue 1 and Ligue 2 70%, WSL 80%, League of Ireland 65%), a salary cap or cost limit (MLS, NWSL, A-League, China, Serie B's soft ceiling, every LALIGA club's official 2026/27 limit and every Turkish club's TFF spending limit), or plain licensing (most leagues, including the ISL, which has no cap for 2026/27 - just don't end a season in debt). The League Rules sheet explains your league's rules with notes and sources; change any of them in Set Up's Override column.
cells.B60: Player data: EA SPORTS FC 27 ratings (EA's ratings API) merged with career-mode potential, value, weekly wage and contract from FUTWIZ and fccareer.ai. Launch data, Sept 2026. FC27 uses Dynamic OVR and growth profiles, so OVR and POT here are launch values - always trust the numbers in your save. Free agents are not in the FC27 database. Money is EUR, wages are weekly.

cells.AP2: SCR replaced PSR from 26/27: squad cost (wages + amortisation + agent fees) must stay within 85% of football revenue + net player-sale profit. Spending above 85% draws a financial levy and uses a multi-year allowance of up to 30% of revenue; beyond that, sporting sanctions. Squad list of 25 with max 17 non-home-grown (home-grown = 3 seasons in England/Wales before 21); U21s need not be listed. No foreign quota - non-UK players need a GBE work permit. Top-to-bottom anchoring was voted down (Nov 2025).
cells.AP3: Championship moved from P&S (GBP 39m / 3 years) to SCR at 85% of income from 26/27, with an owner equity top-up allowance reported at GBP 33m over 3 years (max GBP 15m per season).
cells.AP4: SCMP: player wages limited to 50% of turnover from 26/27, down from 60%. Clubs relegated from the Championship get 65% in their first League One season, down from 75%. Only 50% of owner cash injections can count towards wages. The PFA launched a legal challenge in Aug 2026. Squad list: at most 22 outfield players aged 21+; under-21s and goalkeepers do not count. The 22 or the matchday 18 must include at least one club-developed player, or substitutes are restricted.
cells.AP5: SCMP: player wages limited to 55% of turnover.
cells.AP6: Player salary costs (wages, bonuses, benefits, employer NI, agent fees) capped at 80% of relevant revenue plus owner cash funding up to the higher of 25% of revenue or GBP 4m. Sanctions apply from 2026/27 (2025/26 was a dry run): points deductions of about 1 pt per GBP 100k over. Minimum salary floors per player also apply. League is 14 clubs from 2026/27.
cells.AL7: Scale 0.63 = FC27's median club wage bill (EUR 27.4m) / the real median club player payroll (EUR 43.9m, 2025/26, Capology gross base salaries, adjusted to the 2026/27 line-up, incl. bonuses and social security).
cells.AP7: Each club gets its own squad cost limit (LCPD) from LALIGA - wages, amortisation, agent fees, first team + academy. 2026/27 summer-window limits for every club are loaded automatically (official LALIGA publication, Sept 2026). Max 3 non-EU players.
cells.AL8: Scale 0.45 = FC27's median club wage bill (EUR 4.7m) / the real median club player payroll (EUR 10.6m, 2025/26, FootyStats salary estimates, adjusted to the 2026/27 line-up).
cells.AP8: LCPD per club, loaded automatically for 2026/27. B teams (Real Sociedad B, Celta Fortuna) have no limit of their own and share their parent club's limit. Max 25 first-team licences and max 2 non-EU players. U-23 players from the reserve team can play with shirt numbers 26+.
cells.AP9: Max 25 first-team licences, of which at most 5 non-EU players. At least 6 must be 'players in formation': registered between ages 15 and 21 for 3 seasons at the club or 5 seasons at other Spanish clubs. Reserve-team players can still play when wearing shirt numbers 26 and up. A collective agreement sets a minimum salary. Registration windows run 1 Jul to 18 Sep 2026 and 2 Jan to 2 Feb 2027.
cells.AP10: FIGC extended cost-of-labour indicator: wages + amortisation + agent fees divided by revenue must be at or under 0.7 (from 2026/27, down from 0.8). Wages and amortisation of Under-23 players are left out of the calculation. A club over the limit at the end of a window can only trade at zero net spend unless shareholders cover the gap. Squad list of 25 (players born on or after 1 Jan 2005 are unlimited): at least 8 trained in Italy, of whom at least 4 are club-trained. Up to 2 non-EU signings from abroad per season.
cells.C11: FIGC licensing + LNPB wage thresholds (garanzie integrative)
cells.AL11: Scale 0.21 = FC27's median club wage bill (EUR 2.2m) / the real median club player payroll (EUR 10.6m, 2025/26, Capology gross base salaries). Relegated-club ceilings use Serie A Enilive's scale (0.89) - a relegated club keeps its Serie A Enilive contracts.
cells.AP11: Soft wage ceiling 2026/27 (FIGC CU 225/A): EUR 11m for most clubs; clubs relegated from Serie A get 18m after 3 of their last 4 seasons there, otherwise 14m; newly promoted 7m, second-year promoted 9m (loaded per club). Covers players' and coaches' gross pay and image rights. Going over needs a bank guarantee for 40% of the excess (50% in 2027/28, 60% in 2028/29, 70% from 2029/30; none if the club's liquidity ratio is at least 1). Ceilings fixed through 2029/30. Closed list: max 18 over-23s (+2 'bandiera').
cells.AP12: FC27 has only Juventus (W), Roma (W) from this league. FIGC national licensing (no wage ratio or cap): don't end a season in debt. Non-EU quota for signings from abroad: clubs with no non-EU pros on 30 June can sign up to 3 (the first must be a recent senior international); clubs with 1+ can sign max 2 new non-EU players from abroad per season.
